dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Register the created DC issue for teardown before asserting the binding in `test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers`, so a create-succeeded-but-binding-missing failure does not leak the harness issue.
evidence: `cp = _run(dc_store_copy_repo, _WRITING_MODE, only=local_id)` then `key = load_binding_store(...).get_jira_key(local_id)` then `assert key, (...)` then `track_issue(key)` — the assertion at line 660 precedes the teardown registration at line 666

Every other outbound cell obtains its key via `bound_dc_issue`/`seed_searchable_issue`, both of which call `track_issue(key)` at creation time before any binding assertion (conftest.py:649-651, and seed_searchable_issue in _dc_support.py:180-184)

The failure only leaks when the create DID file an issue but the binding read returns falsy — precisely the binding-persistence defect class the cell's own assert message names ('the outbound pass did not create-and-bind')
dropped.finding: In `test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers`, `track_issue(key)` (which registers the created DC issue for teardown) is called only AFTER the `assert key` binding assertion. If the outbound pass successfully files a harness issue but `get_jira_key(local_id)` returns falsy (the binding-persistence failure class this suite exists to catch), the `assert key` fails and the freshly created harness issue is never registered for teardown, leaking it into the shared instance.
scenarios: A live run where the outbound create files the DC issue but the binding store fails to persist/return the key: the cell fails AND leaves an untracked harness issue behind.
dropped.suggested_fix: Resolve the key and call `track_issue(key)` before the `assert key` check, or wrap the create so any created issue is tracked in a finally/fixture regardless of the binding assertion outcome. If `get_jira_key` returning falsy means no issue was created at all, document that invariant explicitly; otherwise track first.
